public_rationale: The proposed mechanism is plausible: experimental research shows that negative headlines can attract clicks, and worker surveys show widespread concern about AI. Neither source establishes why this particular narrative spread. Combining those general findings would not demonstrate the claimed causal chain from employment fear to engagement to editorial repetition.
limitations: The headline experiments concern another publisher and an earlier period.
Workplace-AI concern is broader than fear of the specific job-loss forecast.
General plausibility is neither confirmation nor contradiction of the stated cause.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The story that AI will eliminate half of white-collar jobs has taken hold because it gets clicks and appeals to a fear everyone has, especially knowledge-economy workers who have long been protected from automation.
conditions: particularly those in the knowledge economy who have long enjoyed protection from automation

statement.excerpt: The “AI is going to eliminate half of white collar jobs” story is one that’s taken hold because it gets clicks and appeals to a fear that everyone, particularly those in the knowledge economy who have long enjoyed protection from automation, has.

from_speaker: has taken hold because it gets clicks
appeals to a fear that everyone
particularly those in the knowledge economy
our_interpretation: The claim attributes the spread of this particular AI job-loss narrative to engagement rewards and employment anxiety.
Everyone is read as ordinary rhetorical emphasis on widespread insecurity, not a literal claim that every person reports the same fear.
Because indicates material contributing causes, not necessarily the only causes.
The assessment concerns the narrative's spread through publication. Its starting date is not specified.
criteria.support_condition: Audience or editorial evidence links greater engagement with this particular narrative to employment fear, and shows that those engagement rewards materially contributed to further coverage.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows that the alleged fear-and-engagement mechanism did not materially contribute to the narrative's spread.

evidence.explanation: Randomized Upworthy headline experiments establish a general engagement mechanism; the event date is the reported end of the analyzed experiment period. They do not test AI employment fears or explain coverage decisions in 2025.

evidence.locator: Section How workers feel about AI use in the workplace
evidence.explanation: The representative survey establishes widespread concern about workplace AI. It does not measure engagement with the half-of-white-collar-jobs story or show that fear caused publishers to amplify it.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Story-specific audience experiments or analytics, paired with evidence about editorial decisions, could establish whether fear-driven engagement materially caused the narrative's spread.
